summary: @onereach/ssml-editor preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package advertises itself as a Vue SSML editor but ships a `preinstall` hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime from the oven-sh/bun GitHub releases URL into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a shipped 727KB single-line file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a heavily obfuscated Bun-CJS bundle (hex-named identifiers, string-array rotator via `push(shift())`, char-code assembly) whose contents cannot be audited from the Node code paths in the package. `setup.mjs` itself is obfuscated with `_0xXXXXXX` identifiers and per-function property-name lookup tables, which is inconsistent with any legitimate native-build lifecycle script. The filename `math_init.js` does not correspond to any mathematical or SSML-editor functionality. On `npm install`, the preinstall hook automatically fetches an alien runtime and executes an opaque obfuscated payload on the installer's machine, matching the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern for smuggling code past Node-focused registry scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
